card.title: Power Vacuum
card.instruction: Treat any uncertainty about who is in charge as an emergency that must be resolved immediately.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nobody's chairing this picnic. We can't open the hamper.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can decide together. I just want everyone fed before the games.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Together isn't a name. The children are opening crisps—who can tell them to wait?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine, you're in charge of lunch. Sam's running the games.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wait. Who's in charge if a game runs into lunch? We need one name now.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 blocks lunch without a chair, A3 demands a single responsible name, and A5 treats overlapping lunch-and-games jurisdictions as an immediate crisis.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's together proposal is explicitly rejected in A3; B4's useful split assignment generates A5's overlap question.

relationship.evidence: B2 seeks timely feeding and B4 offers A real lunch control while assigning games to Sam.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's solution itself to identify the unresolved boundary between two leaders.

specificity.evidence: A1-B2 establish the picnic schedule and A3 the children already eating crisps.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's urgent one-name demand grows from B4's two names without adding an arbitrary new obstacle.
